verdicts.reason: A stacks everything into one column: the shoe is a tiny icon, and the Enter Now CTA and LIMITED badge are miniature pills crammed against the bottom edge under the copy, so the CTA is buried and its text is barely legible. B reads left to right with a clear, prominent CTA at the right. Its flaws: the LIMITED badge leads the composition on the far left, cut off from the product and copy, and the shoe is shrunk to a tiny icon.

A keeps every element, but it is badly cramped: the shoe is tiny and the CTA and badge are minuscule pills jammed at the bottom edge, so the CTA has almost no prominence. B has a strong headline and a clear CTA, but it drops the shoe entirely (the key product image is lost) and squashes the LIMITED badge into an illegible sliver beside the button.

A has the same cramped single column: a buried, tiny CTA and a badge jammed at the bottom edge, plus a postage-stamp shoe. B has a proper banner flow (product, then headline and copy, then a prominent CTA). Its flaws: the shoe is very small, and the LIMITED badge sits tight against the bottom edge with tiny text.

A has a large, readable headline and copy on the left, but the shoe is a tiny sliver, and the Enter Now CTA is a small pill the same weight as the LIMITED badge, so the action is not dominant and its text is near-illegible. B is the cramped single column again: a tiny shoe, a CTA and badge jammed at the bottom edge, and a weak hierarchy.
